chunks: 2461 - He said: And I heard him say:

“Whoever keeps a noble horse, ten sins are erased from him and eleven good deeds are written for him every day. Whoever keeps a mixed-breed horse, two sins are erased from him every day and nine good deeds are written for him every day. Whoever keeps a workhorse, intending by it beauty, fulfilling a need, or repelling an enemy, one sin is erased from him every day and six good deeds are written for him. Whoever keeps a chestnut horse with a white blaze, or one marked on the forehead, then if it is bright-faced, with white on its legs, it is more beloved to me. Poverty will not enter his house so long as that horse is in it, and so long as it remains in the possession of its owner, unfairness will not enter his house.”

key_terms.أَغَرَّ: having a white blaze or brightness on the face
key_terms.بِرْذَوْنًا: a workhorse or heavier riding animal
key_terms.سَيِّئَاتٍ: sins that are erased as a form of divine mercy
key_terms.فَرَسًا: a horse kept or tied by its owner

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the rewards for keeping horses and their effect on poverty?
ai.summary: This hadith describes spiritual reward associated with keeping different kinds of horses, with distinctions based on their quality and intended use. It also praises certain horse features and states that keeping such a horse is linked with protection from poverty and unfairness in the household.
